# The Arbiter Kripke Structure

This notebook is the interactive twin of the arbiter running example from Chapter 7 (Reactive Systems, SMV, and Explicit Model Checking). The arbiter has two state variables, `request` and `state ∈ {Ready, Busy}`, giving four states:

- **RF** — Ready, no request
- **RT** — Ready, request pending
- **BF** — Busy, no request
- **BT** — Busy, request (still) pending

We check the property $\mathbf{AG}(\texttt{request} \to \mathbf{AX}(\texttt{state}=\textsc{Busy}))$: *whenever a request is present, the very next state must be Busy.*

The **buggy** model is the one from the lecture notes: the SMV `case` statement's catch-all `TRUE` branch leaves the arbiter free to go anywhere, so it can silently drop a pending request. The **fixed** model adds one clause — *if already Busy with a request pending, stay Busy* — which is exactly the fix from the chapter's exercises.

## Widget: click through the states

Click any highlighted (reachable) state to take that transition. The property monitor tracks whether $\mathbf{AG}(\texttt{request} \to \mathbf{AX}(\texttt{state}=\textsc{Busy}))$ has been violated *so far* along your run — once violated, it stays violated (violations are safety bugs: no future step can undo them, exactly `def:safety` from the chapter).

```{=html}
<div class="ar-lab" id="nb10-w1">
  <div class="ar-controls">
    <div class="ar-toggle" id="nb10-mode-toggle">
      <button data-mode="buggy" class="active">Buggy model</button>
      <button data-mode="fixed">Fixed model</button>
    </div>
    <button class="ar-btn secondary" id="nb10-reset">Reset</button>
    <button class="ar-btn" id="nb10-showbug">Replay the chapter's counterexample</button>
  </div>

  <div class="ar-workspace">
    <div class="ar-panel">
      <h4>Kripke structure</h4>
      <svg viewBox="0 0 320 260" style="width:100%;height:auto;display:block;" role="img" id="nb10-svg">
        <defs>
          <marker id="nb10-arrow" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="8" refY="3" orient="auto" markerUnits="strokeWidth">
            <path d="M0,0 L0,6 L8,3 z" fill="#303036"></path>
          </marker>
          <marker id="nb10-arrow-bug" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="8" refY="3" orient="auto" markerUnits="strokeWidth">
            <path d="M0,0 L0,6 L8,3 z" fill="#fc5130"></path>
          </marker>
        </defs>
        <g id="nb10-edges"></g>
        <g id="nb10-init-markers"></g>
        <g id="nb10-nodes"></g>
      </svg>
      <div class="ar-current-info" id="nb10-info"></div>
    </div>

    <div class="ar-panel">
      <h4>Property monitor: AG(request &rarr; AX busy)</h4>
      <div id="nb10-verdict"></div>
      <h4 style="margin-top:14px;">Trace so far</h4>
      <div class="ar-trace-strip" id="nb10-trace"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
(function() {
  const NODES = {
    RF: { x: 80,  y: 70,  label: 'RF', ready: true,  request: false },
    RT: { x: 240, y: 70,  label: 'RT', ready: true,  request: true  },
    BF: { x: 80,  y: 200, label: 'BF', ready: false, request: false },
    BT: { x: 240, y: 200, label: 'BT', ready: false, request: true  },
  };

  const BUGGY = {
    RF: ['RF', 'RT', 'BF', 'BT'],
    RT: ['RT', 'RF', 'BF', 'BT'],
    BF: ['BF', 'BT', 'RF', 'RT'],
    BT: ['BT', 'BF', 'RT', 'RF'],
  };
  const FIXED = {
    RF: ['RF', 'RT', 'BF', 'BT'],
    RT: ['RT', 'RF', 'BF', 'BT'],
    BF: ['BF', 'BT', 'RF', 'RT'],
    BT: ['BT', 'BF'],
  };

  let mode = 'buggy';
  let current = 'RF';
  let trace = ['RF'];
  let violated = false;
  let violationStep = -1;

  function transitions() { return mode === 'buggy' ? BUGGY : FIXED; }

  function isViolation(from, to) {
    return NODES[from].request === true && NODES[to].ready === true;
  }

  function step(to) {
    const legal = transitions()[current];
    if (!legal.includes(to)) return;
    if (!violated && isViolation(current, to)) {
      violated = true;
      violationStep = trace.length; // index of the violating state, 1-based step count
    }
    current = to;
    trace.push(to);
    render();
  }

  function reset() {
    current = 'RF';
    trace = ['RF'];
    violated = false;
    violationStep = -1;
    render();
  }

  async function replayBug() {
    reset();
    mode = 'buggy';
    updateModeButtons();
    const script = ['RT', 'BT', 'RT'];
    disableInteraction(true);
    for (const s of script) {
      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 700));
      step(s);
    }
    disableInteraction(false);
  }

  function disableInteraction(disabled) {
    document.querySelectorAll('#nb10-w1 .ar-btn, #nb10-mode-toggle button').forEach(b => b.disabled = disabled);
  }

  function updateModeButtons() {
    document.querySelectorAll('#nb10-mode-toggle button').forEach(b => {
      b.classList.toggle('active', b.dataset.mode === mode);
    });
  }

  function edgePath(a, b, curveOut) {
    const dx = NODES[b].x - NODES[a].x, dy = NODES[b].y - NODES[a].y;
    const mx = (NODES[a].x + NODES[b].x) / 2, my = (NODES[a].y + NODES[b].y) / 2;
    const nx = -dy, ny = dx;
    const len = Math.hypot(nx, ny) || 1;
    const off = curveOut * 18;
    const cx = mx + (nx / len) * off, cy = my + (ny / len) * off;
    return `M ${NODES[a].x} ${NODES[a].y} Q ${cx} ${cy} ${NODES[b].x} ${NODES[b].y}`;
  }

  function render() {
    const legal = transitions()[current];
    const edgesG = document.getElementById('nb10-edges');
    const nodesG = document.getElementById('nb10-nodes');
    const initG = document.getElementById('nb10-init-markers');
    edgesG.innerHTML = '';
    nodesG.innerHTML = '';
    initG.innerHTML = '';

    // initial-state markers on RF and RT
    ['RF', 'RT'].forEach(id => {
      const n = NODES[id];
      const ns = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'line');
      ns.setAttribute('x1', n.x - 40); ns.setAttribute('y1', n.y);
      ns.setAttribute('x2', n.x - 24); ns.setAttribute('y2', n.y);
      ns.setAttribute('stroke', '#999'); ns.setAttribute('stroke-width', '2');
      initG.appendChild(ns);
    });

    // edges from current state to each legal successor
    legal.forEach((to, i) => {
      const isBug = mode === 'buggy' && current === 'BT' && to === 'RT';
      const curve = to === current ? 0 : (i % 2 === 0 ? 1 : -1) * (0.6 + i * 0.15);
      if (to === current) {
        // self-loop: small arc above/right of node
        const n = NODES[current];
        const loop = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path');
        loop.setAttribute('d', `M ${n.x-10} ${n.y-22} C ${n.x-28} ${n.y-46}, ${n.x+28} ${n.y-46}, ${n.x+10} ${n.y-22}`);
        loop.setAttribute('fill', 'none');
        loop.setAttribute('stroke', '#303036');
        loop.setAttribute('stroke-width', '1.6');
        loop.setAttribute('marker-end', 'url(#nb10-arrow)');
        edgesG.appendChild(loop);
        return;
      }
      const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path');
      p.setAttribute('d', edgePath(current, to, curve));
      p.setAttribute('fill', 'none');
      p.setAttribute('stroke', isBug ? '#fc5130' : '#303036');
      p.setAttribute('stroke-width', isBug ? '2.4' : '1.6');
      p.setAttribute('marker-end', isBug ? 'url(#nb10-arrow-bug)' : 'url(#nb10-arrow)');
      edgesG.appendChild(p);
    });

    // nodes
    Object.keys(NODES).forEach(id => {
      const n = NODES[id];
      const g = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'g');
      g.setAttribute('transform', `translate(${n.x},${n.y})`);
      const clickable = legal.includes(id);
      g.setAttribute('class', 'ar-node' + (clickable ? ' clickable' : ''));
      if (clickable) g.addEventListener('click', () => step(id));

      const circle = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'circle');
      circle.setAttribute('r', '26');
      const isCurrent = id === current;
      circle.setAttribute('fill', isCurrent ? '#30bced' : (n.ready ? '#daf3fc' : '#ffe3b3'));
      circle.setAttribute('stroke', n.ready ? '#1f8fb7' : '#e08a00');
      circle.setAttribute('stroke-width', isCurrent ? '3.5' : (clickable ? '2' : '1.2'));
      circle.setAttribute('opacity', clickable || isCurrent ? '1' : '0.35');
      g.appendChild(circle);

      const text = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'text');
      text.setAttribute('text-anchor', 'middle');
      text.setAttribute('dy', '5');
      text.setAttribute('font-weight', '700');
      text.setAttribute('font-family', 'ui-monospace, monospace');
      text.setAttribute('opacity', clickable || isCurrent ? '1' : '0.5');
      text.textContent = n.label;
      g.appendChild(text);

      nodesG.appendChild(g);
    });

    // info line
    const n = NODES[current];
    document.getElementById('nb10-info').innerHTML =
      `Current state: <strong>${current}</strong> &mdash; state = ${n.ready ? 'Ready' : 'Busy'}, request = ${n.request ? 'TRUE' : 'FALSE'}`;

    // verdict
    const verdictEl = document.getElementById('nb10-verdict');
    if (violated) {
      verdictEl.innerHTML = `<div class="ar-verdict-box ar-verdict-fail"><strong>Violated</strong> at step ${violationStep}: a request was pending but the next state was not Busy. This is a finite bad prefix &mdash; no future step can repair it.</div>`;
    } else {
      verdictEl.innerHTML = `<div class="ar-verdict-box ar-verdict-pass">Holds so far. Keep clicking&mdash;in the buggy model, every Busy state with a pending request is one click away from breaking it.</div>`;
    }

    // trace strip
    const traceEl = document.getElementById('nb10-trace');
    traceEl.innerHTML = '';
    trace.forEach(id => {
      const span = document.createElement('span');
      span.className = 'ar-trace-step ' + (NODES[id].ready ? 'ready' : 'busy');
      span.textContent = id;
      traceEl.appendChild(span);
    });
  }

  document.querySelectorAll('#nb10-mode-toggle button').forEach(b => {
    b.addEventListener('click', () => {
      mode = b.dataset.mode;
      updateModeButtons();
      reset();
    });
  });
  document.getElementById('nb10-reset').addEventListener('click', reset);
  document.getElementById('nb10-showbug').addEventListener('click', replayBug);

  render();
})();
</script>
```

## What to try

1. **Reproduce the bug manually.** Starting from `RF`, click `RT` (a request arrives), then `BT` (the arbiter correctly goes Busy), then `RT` again. The monitor should flag a violation on that last click&mdash;this is exactly the counterexample $\textsf{RF} \to \textsf{RT} \to \textsf{BT} \to \textsf{RT}$ from the chapter (`ex:arbiter-safety-ce`).
2. **Switch to the fixed model** and try to reproduce the same violation from `BT`. You can't&mdash;`BT`'s only legal successors are `BF` and `BT` itself, so a pending request can never be silently dropped.
3. **Try an existential query by hand.** Can you reach `BF` from `RF` without ever passing through a state with `request = TRUE`? (Yes&mdash;`RF → BF` directly, in one click, in *either* model.) That is the same shape of question as $\mathbf{EF}(\texttt{state}=\textsc{Busy} \land \neg\texttt{request})$ from the chapter's existential-model-checking example, and here you can find the witness yourself.
